description: §14.8.9 raw-egress fail-closed — a BRACKET access with a static string key denotes exactly the property the dot form denotes, so `new globalThis["Response"](...)` fires E-PROTECT-004 identically to `new globalThis.Response(...)` and to a bare `new Response(...)`. Pins the fix for a measured fail-open in the structural detector's FIRST cut: `a["b"]` parses to an INDEX node (types/ast.ts — `MemberExpr.property` is a plain string, computed access is `IndexExpr`), which the callee resolver did not resolve, so this exact file compiled at exit 0 with ZERO diagnostics and the emitted handler, executed, answered `{"id":1,"name":"ada","passwordHash":"$argon2id$SECRET"}`. The bracket forms `window["Response"]`, `globalThis["foo"]["Response"]`, `globalThis["Response"].json(...)` and `Response["json"](...)` all reach the same conclusion.
rationale: §14.8.9's closed-world precondition (SPEC.md:8519-8525) puts the SHALL on the CONSTRUCT — 'a manual `Response` / `handle()` body (§40)' — not on a spelling of it, so a detector that recognises one surface form and not another under-enforces the normative rule. A bracket with a string-literal key is STATICALLY RESOLVABLE: the key's value is on the `lit` node the parser already built, so reading it is the tree's own answer, not a re-scan of source text (invariant 55). The bound this case states is that the key's VALUE must be in the tree. That bound was FALSE as first written, and is now true: `new globalThis["Resp" + "onse"](JSON.stringify(u))` compiled at exit 0 with ZERO diagnostics on every tree and its executed handler shipped the secret, because the concatenation was not folded — yet both operands are literals sitting in the tree, so the key was never dynamic. `staticIndexKey` now folds a `+` of static string keys recursively (S354), and the fold is STRING-only so `a[1 + 1]` is still not a key. The genuine residual is a key whose value is not in the tree at all (`let k = "Response"; globalThis[k]`, an interpolated template, a call result) — that needs the name resolver / constant propagation, and it is stated as a bound in `collectRawEgressFacts` / `detectProtectedRawEgressAcrossFns` rather than claimed closed. provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S352 (dpa-029 Q1).
